messages:
kyle_customer: Hey team — since yesterday our Private deployment behind corp-proxy is intermittently failing on model calls. Clients get TLS handshake errors or 502s. Happening only when route goes through our enterprise proxy (Zscaler).

kyle_customer: Repro steps we used: 
1) from our bastion (uses corp-proxy):
   curl -v --proxy http://corp-proxy.company:8080 https://private.redwood.company/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>'
   -> sometimes returns HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway, other times TLS handshake errors in client logs.

kyle_customer: From same host, bypassing proxy (direct egress) works fine. We suspect proxy is doing TLS inspection / CONNECT handling weirdness.

anna_support: Sorry you're hitting this, Kyle. Can you paste the curl -v output (trim secrets) and the client TLS error (stack or openssl output) so we can see if SNI or cert mismatch is present? Also which proxy vendor + version?

kyle_customer: Here's a snip (sanitized):
```
> CONNECT private.redwood.company:443 HTTP/1.1
> Host: private.redwood.company:443
> Proxy-Authorization: Basic <redacted>
< HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established
* CONNECT phase completed
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS alert, Server hello (2):
* SSL: error:1400442E:SSL routines:openssl_internal:tlsv1 alert internal error
* Closing connection 0
```

kyle_customer: The proxy logs show it unwraps and re-signs certs (SSL inspection). Vendor: Zscaler (cloud). Policy has "ssl inspection" enabled for web categories.

raj_devops: Zscaler doing TLS inspection will replace SNI / re-encrypt using its own certs — that should be fine usually, but some gateways rewrite Host headers or strip SNI to route by IP. If SNI is removed/rewritten the backend sees wrong servername, and cert hostname mismatch can happen when proxy rewrites host header but not SNI, or vice versa.

raj_devops: Quick checks:
- Run `openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.company:443 -servername private.redwood.company` from inside the bastion both with and without proxy: that shows whether the proxy preserves SNI. If the server certificate CN/SAN doesn't match the hostname, you'll see it.
- For CONNECT-tunneled traffic: `curl --proxy http://corp-proxy:8080 -v --resolve private.redwood.company:443:203.0.113.10 https://private.redwood.company/v1/models` to force connect to the expected IP and show proxy behavior.

anna_support: Also check if Zscaler is performing active MITM and re-issuing certs: do you see Zscaler in the certificate chain? That would confirm TLS decryption is happening. If so, ask your security team to add an exception (SSL inspection bypass) for private.redwood.company and related domains or create a CONNECT passthrough rule for port 443 to our hostnames.

lisa_infra: Another vector we've seen: some proxies rewrite the Host header on the upstream request after terminating TLS, which can break route-based cert selection on our edge (SNI expects one hostname, Host header gets changed). If your proxy is doing header normalization or is applying a URI mapping rule, that could cause 502s when our gateway receives a mismatched Host header.

kyle_customer: Ok we confirmed Zscaler is in the chain. How specific does the allowlist need to be? Our security team is strict about wide bypass rules.

anna_support: Prefer a hostname-level bypass for your private deployment: `private.redwood.company` and any subdomains used for model endpoints and control plane (e.g., *.dedicated.redwood.company). If wildcard bypass isn't allowed, list the exact hostnames you call. Also allow CONNECT with tunnel mode (no SSL inspection) for those hosts.

raj_devops: If policy changes are slow, a temporary workaround: configure your proxy to allow CONNECT pass-through for 443 to the target IP(s). That keeps the TLS handshake end-to-end. Command we often ask customers to run to prove it: `curl -v --proxy http://corp-proxy:8080 https://private.redwood.company/health` and compare the certificate subject. If you get our leaf cert (not Zscaler-signed), TLS passthrough succeeded.

proxybot: [automated hint] Common enterprise proxies that default to SSL inspection: Zscaler, BlueCoat/ProxySG, Palo Alto, F5 ASM. Look for settings named "SSL Inspection", "SSL Forward Proxy", or "TLS Decryption".

kyle_customer: Security team says they can add an exception for `private.redwood.company` but need the list of hostnames used by the Private deployment (control plane vs data plane). Also they asked if Redwood can support SNI-less clients.

anna_support: We'll provide a minimal hostname list (DM in a sec). We do not recommend serving without SNI—it breaks multi-tenant cert routing on our side. We can file an engineering ticket to see if we can be more tolerant, but the supported fix is to disable TLS inspection / enable passthrough for the hostnames.

lisa_infra: Action items: (1) Kyle - confirm exact hostnames/IPs to add to Zscaler bypass; (2) Support -> send docs + recommended curl/openssl commands; (3) Eng-infra to triage if customer remains blocked after bypass (we may need to check gateway logs).

kyle_customer: Got it. Will follow up with security and paste the Zscaler ACL once they respond. Thanks for the debugging steps.

anna_support: Thanks — please include any proxy config snippets or packet capture TLS ClientHello/ServerHello (redacted) if you can. We'll keep this thread open and escalate to eng-infra if you still see 502s after the bypass.
